entry.title: On Cayley Graphs of Skew Braces and Their Distances
entry.summary: We introduce the left and right Cayley graphs of a finite skew brace $(A,\cdot, \circ)$ with a connection set $T\subset A$, as a directed multigraph with additive and multiplicative edges, depicting the operations $\cdot$ and $\circ$ respectively. We compute the distance from $a$ to $a\circ b$ in these Cayley graphs in terms of factorization lengths over $T$. As an application, we provide a characterization of the ideals of a skew brace in terms of their corresponding Cayley graphs.

entry.title: Maximum length and size of simultaneous core partitions with distinct parts
entry.summary: We give, for the first time, a formula for the largest size of an $(s,t)$-core partition with distinct parts valid for every coprime pair. We also determine the greatest number of parts of an $(s,t)$-core partition whose successive parts differ by at least $D$, whenever $\gcd(s,t)\le D$, removing the restrictions on the core parameters in the formula of Burson, Sisneros-Thiry, and Straub. The size formula uses a column description and a single Dedekind sum. The length formula uses coefficients from the Euclidean algorithm and satisfies a recurrence in smaller core parameters. We construct partitions attaining each maximum.

entry.title: A generalization of pseudocomplementation in semilattices, lattices and posets with 0
entry.summary: Pseudocomplemented lattices satisfy a lot of nice properties and were studied by a number of algebraists. However, even when a poset P with 0 is not pseudocomplemented, we can assign to every element a of P the set $a^p$ of all maximal elements being orthogonal to a. This assignment $^p$ is a non-trivial operator provided P satisfies the so-called Ascending Chain Condition (ACC). In particular, we investigate this operator when the poset P in question is a semilattice or a lattice. We characterize this operator and describe its properties that turn out to be similar to the corresponding properties of pseudocomplementation. Moreover, we introduce an equivalence relation $Θ_p$ on P induced by $^p$ similarly as it was done by V. I. Glivenko for distributive pseudocomplemented lattices. Finally, we investigate for which lattices L with 0 satisfying the ACC this equivalence relation turns out to be a congruence and when the quotient lattice $L/Θ_p$ is complemented respectively modular.

entry.title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
entry.summary: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $α$, let $λ_{k,α}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24λ_{k,α}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^α}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^αn+λ_{k,α}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(α+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.

entry.title: Scott-type inequalities for trinomial $h^*$-polynomials
entry.summary: Motivated by Scott's inequality for lattice polygons, we study normalized volume bounds for lattice polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ with $h^*$-polynomials $1+at^k+bt^\ell$, where $a,b\ge1$ and $1\le k<\ell$. For $\ell>2k$, the coefficients satisfy $a+1\le b$, and consequently ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le2b$. In the complementary range $k<\ell\le2k$, we establish the dimension-independent bound \[ {\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le(2b+1)(k+\ell). \] On the boundary $\ell=2k$ with $b\ge2$, the sharper Scott-type inequality ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le4k(b+1)$ holds, confirming a conjecture of Higashitani, Nill, and the author. Equality holds if and only if $k=1$ and $a=3b+3$. Moreover, when $\ell=2k$ and $k,b\ge2$, we obtain an upper bound depending only on $b$.

entry.title: Regular Graphs Without Isomorphic Bisections
entry.summary: A graph is bisectable if its vertex set can be split into two sets inducing isomorphic subgraphs. Ando conjectured that every cubic graph is bisectable, and Das, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov proved it for large enough connected cubic graphs. We give a constructive proof that, for every $d\geq5$, there exists a non-bisectable $d$-regular graph of even order.

entry.title: Combinatorial decompositions of strict partitions and multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities
entry.summary: While multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities have been extensively investigated through Bailey pairs, the constant term method, complex contour integration, and related techniques, many still lack an intrinsic combinatorial understanding. In this paper, we establish combinatorial interpretations for several families of triple-sum identities via structural decompositions of strict partitions. For one of these families, we extend the underlying combinatorial framework to obtain a general $(m+1)$-fold multi-sum identity. Leveraging these partition-theoretic interpretations, we construct explicit bijective proofs for all the corresponding identities. As an application, this constructive approach naturally yields some parameterized generalizations.

entry.title: Optimal $K_t$-free list colorings and the Pollyanna property of graphs with no triangular wheel
entry.summary: A wheel consists of an induced cycle of length at least four and a vertex with at least three neighbors on the cycle. Let $\cal T$ be the class of graphs with no wheel containing a triangle. We prove that, for every $G\in\cal T$ and every integer $t\ge3$, the $K_t$-free chromatic and choice numbers both equal $\lceil{ω(G)/(t-1)}\rceil$. We further prove that $\cal T$ is $k$-strongly linear-Pollyanna for every integer $k\ge2$, and hence is linear-Pollyanna. In particular, the class of wheel-free graphs is Pollyanna, answering Problem 10.2 of Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies and Oum.

entry.title: Falconer estimate for circular and cinematic Furstenberg problem
entry.summary: We prove the Falconer-type bound $\dim_{\mathrm H}F\geq u+1$ for planar circular $(u,v)$-Furstenberg sets whenever $0<u\leq1$, $0<v\leq3$, and $2u+v\geq3$. The same bound holds for smooth cinematic curve families. This resolves the circular Furstenberg conjecture of Green, Harris, Ou, Ren, and Tammen in its full Falconer range $2u+v\geq3$.

entry.title: Sharp Bounds for Graph-Codes Avoiding Complete Bipartite Differences
entry.summary: Let $d_{K_{s,t}}(n)$ be the largest fraction of all graphs on $[n]$ in a family containing no two distinct members whose symmetric difference is a copy of $K_{s,t}$. We determine this maximum density for every fixed pair of positive integers $s,t$. If both part sizes are odd, it is known that the density is exactly $1/2$. Otherwise, let $2h$ be the largest even part size. We prove $$ d_{K_{s,t}}(n)=Θ_{s,t}(n^{-h}). $$ For $h>1$, this improves the general $O_{s,t}(1/n)$ upper bound obtained from Alon's two-copy gluing theorem~\cite{Alon2024}. The sharp bounds for even stars were already proved by Alon and are recovered as special cases. The upper bound uses the Frankl--Füredi forbidden-intersection theorem. For the lower bound, we construct binary linear codes using BCH codes. When exactly one part size is even, we assign to each edge the sum of the binary vectors assigned to its endpoints. When both part sizes are even, we identify these vectors with elements of a finite field and assign to each edge the product of its endpoint elements. In both cases, every copy of $K_{s,t}$ has a nonzero syndrome.

entry.title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
entry.summary: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

entry.title: Two families of Young tableaux with periodic walls: Counting formulas and differential transcendence
entry.summary: Banderier, Marchal, and Wallner studied the enumeration problem for Young tableaux with walls. These are similar to standard Young tableaux, except that local decreases are allowed at some walls. In 2021, Banderier and Wallner counted Young tableaux with periodic walls, in which the elementary blocks are Young diagrams of shape $(2,2)$. They obtained exact counting formulas for $30$ of the $32$ classes up to symmetry. In this paper, we first derive recurrences for counting the remaining two classes of Young tableaux with periodic walls. We then prove that their counting exponential generating functions are differentially transcendental. Consequently, they are neither D-algebraic nor D-finite. This disproves a conjecture of Banderier and Wallner.

entry.title: A Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs
entry.summary: Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type conditions are degree conditions for the existence of hamiltonian cycles in digraphs, which impose degree restrictions on nonadjacent vertices which have a common in-neighbor or a common out-neighbor. They can be viewed as directed analogues of both Fan-type conditions and heavy subgraph conditions in undirected graphs, and they also generalized the classes of locally semicomplete digrahs, loclaly in-semicomplete digraphs, and locally out-semicomplete digraphs. In this paper, we prove what is, to our knowledge, the first Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs. More precisely, let $D$ be a strong digraph with order $n\ge 3$. We show that, if for every $u\in V(D)$ belonging to a dominated nonadjacent pair or a dominating nonadjacent pair, we have $d(u)\ge n$, then $D$ is pancyclic, unless $D$ belongs to one of two well-characterized classes of exceptional digraphs.

entry.title: Solid-Resolving Sets on Directed Graphs
entry.summary: A set $S \subseteq V(G)$ is a solid-resolving set of an undirected graph $G$ if each vertex can be distinguished from any vertex subset by their distances from the set $S$. Solid-resolving sets are a generalization of resolving sets, which have been studied extensively in the literature. We extend this concept to oriented graphs and directed graphs. In this setting, we first define solid-resolving sets for digraphs and then consider vertices that must be included in any solid-resolving set. We also study the solid-metric dimension, which is the minimum cardinality of a solid-resolving set of a given digraph. We determine the possible values of the solid-metric dimension for several common graph classes, including tournaments, directed trees, oriented cycles, complete bipartite graphs, as well as for Cartesian products of oriented paths and cycles. We also show via some examples that there is no trivial relation between the solid-metric dimension of a digraph and the solid-metric dimension of its underlying undirected graph. Furthermore, we show that the solid-metric dimension can increase or decrease by an arbitrary $k$ when one vertex is removed. Similarly, removing a single arc can decrease the solid-metric dimension by an arbitrary $k$; however, it can increase by at most 1. The arbitrary changes in solid-metric dimension indicate that the solid-metric dimension is a global, rather than a local, property.
entry.arxiv:comment: 24 pages, 5 figures. This paper has been presented in part in IWOCA 2026

entry.title: Multiple harmonic star sums involving central binomial coefficients as weights
entry.summary: We consider weighted analogues of multiple harmonic and multiple $t$-harmonic star sums, where the "star" indicates non-strict inequalities between the summation indices. In the special case where all exponents are 2, which is of particular interest also for ordinary multiple ($t$-)harmonic star sums, we obtain evaluations in terms of simple finite sums. The proofs are based on several combinatorial identities which are of interest in their own right.

entry.title: The Choice Number of Random Graphs
entry.summary: In 1999, Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov conjectured that the choice number and chromatic number of the random graph $G(n,p)$ are asymptotically equal whenever $np\to\infty$. We prove their conjecture, showing that, with high probability, $$ \operatorname{ch}(G(n,p))=(1+o(1))χ(G(n,p)) $$ whenever $np\to\infty$. This improves the bound $\operatorname{ch}(G(n,p))\le(2+o(1))χ(G(n,p))$ for $np\to\infty$ and $p\le0.9$ obtained by Krivelevich and Vu in 2001. Our proof distinguishes two cases according to the size of independent sets. When independent sets of growing size are available, we establish a sharper uniform independent-set estimate that eliminates the factor-two loss in the bound of Krivelevich and Vu. When independent sets have bounded size, we establish a deterministic result showing that, under a suitable uniform independent-set condition, a proper colouring with bounded colour-class sizes yields an asymptotically matching upper bound on the choice number.

entry.title: Saturation numbers of $K_3 \vee P_k$
entry.summary: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-saturated if $G$ contains no copy of $H$, but $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$ for any edge $e$ of $\overline{G}$. The saturation number of $H$, denoted by $\mathrm{sat}(n, H)$, is the minimum number of edges among all $H$-saturated graphs of order $n$. In this paper, we investigate the saturation number of $K_3 \vee P_k$ for $k \ge 3$ and show that $\mathrm{sat}(n, K_3 \vee P_k) = 3n - 6 + \mathrm{sat}(n-3, P_k)$ holds for all $n \ge a_k + 3$ and $k \ge 3$, which verifies the conjecture [Discrete Appl. Math, 394(2026) 62-80] on $\mathrm{sat}(n, K_s \vee P_k)$ is true for the case $s=3$, where $a_k = k$ for $3 \le k \le 5$, $a_k = 3 \cdot 2^{t-1} - 2$ for $k = 2t \ge 6$, and $a_k = 2^{t+1} - 2$ for $k = 2t + 1 \ge 7$.

entry.title: Upper bounding the coefficients of Tutte polynomials with a variable fixed
entry.summary: The Tutte polynomial is a fundamental invariant of graphs and matroids. For a matroid M of rank r, the Tutte polynomial T_M(x,y) of M serves as a generalization of the characteristic polynomial chi_M(x), with the relationship given by chi_M(x) = (-1)^r T_M(1-x,0). For any real number t satisfying 0 <= t <= 1, under suitable exclusion hypotheses on M, we establish an upper bound on the coefficients of the polynomial T_M(x,t) (resp., T_M(t,y)) in terms of girth g and the number of circuits of size g (resp., maximum cardinality h of hyperplanes and the number of hyperplanes of size h). The resulting characteristic polynomial bound extends the bound of Delaplane and Wu [Discrete Math. 312(12-13) (2012) 2062-2068] to simple U_{g-1,g+1}-free matroids satisfying n >= r + c_g, thereby giving a partial affirmative answer to the question of extending their upper bound beyond binary matroids.

entry.title: Exponentially large mu-coefficients
entry.summary: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.

entry.title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
entry.summary: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.

entry.title: The flag major index on conjugacy classes of wreath products
entry.summary: A classical result, independently proved by Garsia and by Wachs, gives a simple and elegant closed expression for the evaluation, at a primitive root of unity, of the major index generating function over a conjugacy class in the symmetric group. In this paper, we generalize this result to the flag major index generating function over conjugacy classes in any wreath product $\mathbb{Z}_{r}\wr S_{n}$. Our approach is new, and applies conjugation by a Coxeter element as a cyclic group action on the conjugacy class. This leads to a simple formula in the general case.

entry.title: On the product of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
entry.summary: Let $n\geq2\ell\geq2k\geq6$ and $n>k+\ell$. We determine the maximum of $|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|$ over all nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families $\mathcal A\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ and $\mathcal B\subseteq\binom{[n]}\ell$. The exact bound is $|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\leq\max\{M_1,M_2\}$, where \[ \begin{aligned} M_1 &=\left(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-\ell-1}{k-1}+1\right) \left(\binom{n-1}{\ell-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{\ell-1}+1\right),\\ M_2 &=\left(\binom{n-2}{\ell-2}+1\right) \sum_{i=1}^{2} \left(\binom{n-i}{k-1}-\binom{n-\ell-i}{k-1}\right). \end{aligned} \] Both terms are attained by explicit constructions: a Hilton--Milner-type pair and a two-point construction, respectively. We classify all equality cases, including the additional cross-triangle pairs when $k=\ell=3$. Two structural results underlie the proof. First, we establish a restricted-lex comparison theorem showing that restricted lexicographic initial segments minimize disjointness neighborhoods, and characterize equality at the first nontrivial threshold. Second, a decomposition of critically shifted families into two parts with disjoint cores leads to a sharp product theorem, with equality characterized, for all cross-intersecting pairs admitting this decomposition, without additional nontriviality assumptions. Endpoint comparisons and reverse shifting complete the proof for unequal as well as equal uniformities.

entry.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
entry.summary: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanović's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.
entry.arxiv:comment: 45 pages, includes computer-assisted proofs and supplementary Python/SageMath verification programs

entry.title: Cross work induced by transformations on the symmetric group and related transformation semigroups
entry.summary: We introduce a new permutation statistic, called the \emph{cross work}, on four important subsemigroups of the partial transformation semigroup $\mathcal{PT}_n$: the symmetric group $\mathcal{S}_n$, the semigroup of singular transformations $\mathrm{Sing}_n$, the symmetric inverse semigroup $\mathcal{I}_n$, and the semigroup $\mathcal{POI}_n$ of partial order-preserving injective transformations. The cross work is defined via local distance interactions between adjacent positions and their images. Fundamental invariance properties are established, including inversion invariance under a natural symmetry condition and a characterization of conjugations preserving the statistic. Using elementary combinatorial methods, we derive closed formulas for the total and average cross work on $\mathcal{S}_n$. We also determine the exact minimum and maximum values of the cross work, showing that the maximal value grows quadratically with $n$.
entry.arxiv:comment: 20 pages. An article by Nsibiet E. Udo, Victor A. Owai and Moses O. Francis

entry.title: Rainbow maps and the number of graceful labelings of trees
entry.summary: Let $τ(N)$ be the number of graceful labelings of trees with $N$ edges, that is, the number of spanning trees of the complete graph on $\{0,1,\dots,N\}$ whose edges have distinct lengths. The answer to exercise 7.2.2.3-106 of The Art of Computer Programming states that, if an empirical observation of Anick is true, then $τ(n)=\exp(n\ln n-n\ln(e/b)+O(\log n))$ with $b\approx0.636$, and that rigorous proofs are unknown. We prove that $|\logτ(N)-(N\log N-N\log(e/b))|\le152(1+\log(N+1))^4$ for every $N\ge3$, with $b=2/π$. A rainbow map of order $N$ sends each vertex $k\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$ to a vertex $f(k)\in\{0,\dots,N\}$ so that the lengths $|f(k)-k|$ are $1,\dots,N-1$ in some order. Acyclic rainbow maps are exactly the graceful labelings, and all rainbow maps are counted by the Whitty numbers $W(N)$ (OEIS A134983). We show that $τ(N)\le W(N)\leτ(N)e^{151(1+\log(N+1))^4}$ by a combinatorial argument: for fixed directions, rainbow maps are rook placements on a Ferrers board; a swap injection shows that a uniformly random rainbow map has $O(\log^2N)$ cycles on average; and an inequality on the periods of a word shows that the $c$ cycles of a rainbow map can be removed by changing $O(c\log N)$ edges. We also show that $W(N)$ is the total weight of a family of weighted Motzkin paths. This yields exact enumerations, an alternating sum for $W(N)$, and a representation of $W(N)$ as a moment of a continuous dual Hahn weight, from which $|\log W(N)-(N\log(2N/π)-N)|\le5(1+\log(N+1))$. The main theorem has been formalized in Lean 4; its combinatorial half uses no axioms beyond those of Lean.
entry.arxiv:comment: 27 pages, 2 figures. A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem is included in the ancillary files (directory anc/lean)

entry.title: On strong odd colorings of sparse graphs
entry.summary: A strong odd coloring of a graph is a proper vertex coloring such that for every vertex $v$, each color appearing on the neighborhood of $v$ appears an odd number of times. We investigate strong odd colorings of sparse graphs, where sparsity of a graph $G$ is measured in terms of maximum average degree, denoted $\operatorname{mad}(G)$. We prove that the optimal threshold on the maximum average degree guaranteeing a strong odd $c$-coloring is $4-Θ(\frac{1}{c})$ as $c\to\infty$. Moreover, for every $c\geq 5$, this threshold is strictly smaller than the threshold for odd $c$-coloring. We also determine the sharp threshold on the maximum average degree guaranteeing a strong odd $5$-coloring: every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{mad}(G)<\frac{7}{3}$ has a strong odd $5$-coloring, and this bound is sharp. In addition, we show that every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{mad}(G)<\frac{11}{5}$ and no induced $5$-cycle has a strong odd $4$-coloring. Note that the $5$-cycle has maximum average degree 2 and no strong odd $4$-coloring.

entry.title: Average eccentricity in k-connected tournaments
entry.summary: The average eccentricity $\avec(D)$ of a strong digraph $D$ is the mean eccentricity of all vertices in $D$. A tournament $T$ is an orientation of a complete graph. In this paper, we prove that the average eccentricity satisfies $2 \le \avec(T) < \frac{n}{2k} + \frac{11}{2} + \frac{k}{8n}$ for a $k$-connected tournament $T$ of order $n$. We further examine the case for strong tournaments where $k = 1$, and show that $\avec(T) \le \frac{n+11}{2} + \frac{1}{8n}$ for any strong tournament $T$. Moreover, we show that the lower bound $2$ is sharp and that the upper bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant.

entry.title: The $e$-expansion of integral form Macdonald polynomials
entry.summary: In this paper, we investigate the expansion of the integral form Macdonald polynomials $J_μ(x;q,t)$ in the elementary symmetric function basis. Motivated by the connection between chromatic symmetric functions and LLT polynomials, we conjecture the $e$-positivity of a normalization of $J_μ(x;q,t)$. We verify the conjecture when $μ$ is either a hook or a two-column partition. In the hook case, we express the $e$-coefficients as weighted sums over compositions. In the two-column case, we derive explicit formulas for the $e$-coefficients.

entry.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
entry.summary: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $Δ(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $Δ(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

entry.title: A proof of the Grothendieck join-meet positivity
entry.summary: We prove the (signed) Grothendieck join--meet positivity $$ G_{λ\veeμ}G_{λ\wedgeμ} -G_λG_μ\in \sum_ν \mathbb{N}\cdot (-1)^{|ν|-|λ|-|μ|}G_ν$$ for stable Grothendieck polynomials using geometric Satake equivalence, thereby resolving a conjecture posed by Thomas and Yong.

entry.title: Dual near-factorizations and Schur products in association schemes
entry.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be Gram matrices of spherical $2$-designs on the same number of indices. We study when their Schur product is again the Gram matrix of a spherical design. We give a criterion in terms of orthogonal projections with constant diagonal, and an explicit $15$-point spherical $3$-design whose Gram matrix belongs to no symmetric Bose-Mesner algebra. For a symmetric association scheme, the factorization problem takes the form $v(E_S\circ E_T)=μE_U$. This is a counterpart of ordinary matrix product factorizations in the adjacency basis. The case $E_U=I-E_0$ gives a dual near-factorization and has a regular simplex as its normalized output. We characterize complementary input supports by a strongly regular fusion, give a reciprocal criterion, and classify the case in which one factor is the last Hamming idempotent.

entry.title: Correlation inequalities for volume polynomials
entry.summary: We establish sharp correlation inequalities for volume polynomials associated with covers of multisets. These inequalities simultaneously generalize the Khovanskii--Teissier and reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities for intersections of nef divisor classes on projective varieties. They also hold for volume polynomials arising from convex bodies and Hermitian matrices, recovering and extending classical results such as the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes of convex bodies and the Hadamard--Fischer inequality for determinants of positive semidefinite matrices. As a combinatorial application, we prove a negative correlation inequality for partitions of bases of matroids that are linearly realizable over a field.

entry.title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
entry.summary: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.

entry.title: On the frieze patterns by Conway and Coxeter
entry.summary: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s. Since then the theory of frieze patterns exploded with new results, and frieze patterns found a wide spectrum of connections in various domains of mathematics, including combinatorics, geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. The literature on frieze patterns grew vastly and continues to expand. In this note we give a brief overview of some of the directions emerging from the papers by Conway and Coxeter and single out core ideas which were later replayed in different contexts.
entry.arxiv:comment: This survey was written in November 2025 for the prospected book with a tentative title 'The Conway Book', in preparation

entry.title: A graded version of the separator theorem for planar graphs
entry.summary: We prove that every planar graph on $n$ vertices has a vertex ordering $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n$ in which each prefix $\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}$ is joined to at most $C\sqrt{i}$ elements of $\{v_{i+1},\ldots,v_n\}$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. Consequently, every prefix can be separated from its complement by deleting $O\left(\sqrt{i}\right)$ vertices lying entirely in its complement.

entry.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$
entry.summary: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/π^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Apéry-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.

entry.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
entry.summary: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

entry.title: Envy-Free Allocations for Random Non-Additive Valuations
entry.summary: Benade et al. (EC 2024) introduced a semi-random model for non-additive fair division in which each agent starts with an arbitrary base valuation over bundles of items and independently permutes the item names uniformly at random. While they proved that envy-free allocations exist with high probability as the number of items grows for $n = 2$ agents, they left open whether the same holds for $n > 2$ agents. We resolve this open question in the affirmative: for any fixed number of agents $n$ and any number of items $m$ divisible by $n$, an envy-free allocation exists with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $m \to \infty$. Our proof combines the second moment method with a connection to the (small-set) expansion of generalized Johnson graphs, which may be of independent interest.

entry.title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
entry.summary: Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets. A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $Ω((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

entry.title: Online Discrepancy of Sparse Random Vectors over Long Horizons
entry.summary: We study online vector balancing for independent sparse random vectors: each arrival is supported on a uniformly random set of $s$ of the $n$ coordinates, with nonzero entries equal to one (binary model) or independent random signs (signed model), and an online algorithm must sign each vector upon arrival. The prefix discrepancy is the largest $\ell_\infty$-norm of the signed sums up to the horizon $T$, the terminal discrepancy that of the sum at time $T$. For binary inputs with $2\le s\le n/2$ and $T=Θ(n)$, Altschuler and Tikhomirov showed that both are of order $\sqrt{s}+\log\log n$; they asked how the prefix discrepancy depends on the horizon and whether a matching terminal bound holds at every prescribed time. Over long horizons, the two differ. For every fixed $s\ge2$ and $c>0$, every online algorithm, even a randomized one that knows the horizon, incurs with high probability prefix discrepancy $Ω(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{α_s})$ for $n\le T\le e^{cn}$, where $α_s=(2^{s-1}-1)/(2^s-1)$. For $s=2$, quadratic Greedy matches this bound; for fixed $s\ge3$, we give an online algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{1/2})$. In contrast, a deterministic algorithm that knows neither the horizon nor the failure probability keeps the terminal discrepancy $O_k(\sqrt{s}+\log\log n)$ at each prescribed time, with failure probability $n^{-k}$ for every fixed $k$, for $2\le s\le n/2$ (binary model) and $2\le s\le n$ (signed model); for $s=2$, quadratic Greedy itself does so. This answers their terminal question, and the same order is optimal for prefixes at all polynomial horizons $T\ge n$. The lower bound uses a finite safety game realized within the input law; the upper bounds use moments of elementary symmetric polynomials and, at terminal times, a $\cosh$ potential or a translated gauge with a Foster inequality at every state.

entry.title: The Plane-Saturation Ratio of Planar Graphs
entry.summary: For a planar graph \(G\), a plane subgraph \(H\) is plane-saturated with respect to \(G\) if adding any edge to the fixed drawing of \(H\), possibly together with new vertices, either creates a crossing or results in a graph that is not a subgraph of \(G\). The plane-saturation ratio \(\psr(G)\) is the minimum of \(e(H)/e(G)\) over all plane-saturated subgraphs \(H\) of \(G\). For nonnegative integers \(k_1\) and \(k_2\), let \(\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) denote the class of planar graphs in which, for each \(i\in\{1,2\}\), at most \(k_i\) vertices of degree \(i\) have any prescribed neighborhood, where \(k_i=0\) means that vertices of degree \(i\) are forbidden. We prove that every \(G\in\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) with at least one edge satisfies $\psr(G)>\frac{1}{9+k_1+6k_2}.$ This settles two conjectures of Clifton and Salia.

entry.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
entry.summary: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.
entry.arxiv:comment: 39 pages. Revised exposition and organisation, with expanded explanations. Main results and theorem statements unchanged

entry.title: Counting Admissible Sets of Integers: A Proof of the Erdős--Nicolas--Sárközy Conjecture
entry.summary: A finite set of positive integers is admissible if any two of its subsets with the same sum have the same cardinality. In 1991, Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy conjectured that $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$, where $a(N)$ denotes the number of nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. We prove this conjecture by showing that there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that $\exp(c\sqrt N)\le a(N)\le\exp(C\sqrt N)$ for every integer $N\ge4$. The same bounds hold for the number of admissible sets with maximum $N$. For the upper bound, we show that every sufficiently large admissible set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains a subset of proportional size whose doubling constant is $O(N/|A|^2)$.

entry.title: A general algebraic characterization of extremal $Δ$-trees and $k$-cyclic graphs for degree-homogeneous VDB indices
entry.summary: We present a general algebraic method for maximizing a vertex-degree-based (VDB) topological index $TI(G) = \sum_{uv \in E(G)} f(d(u),d(v))$ over the class of $n$-vertex trees with a prescribed maximum degree $Δ\ge 3$. By expressing the edge multiplicities of the basis $\mathcal{B} = \{(1,Δ), (Δ,Δ)\}$ via degree-sum identities, we reduce the maximization of $TI(T)$ to the minimization of an explicit discrete penalty function $G(x,y)$ over the non-basic edges. We formulate five analytical conditions on the weight function $f(x,y)$ that dictate the optimal edge distributions, yielding a complete characterization of the extremal trees across all congruence classes of $n \pmod{Δ- 1}$. Additionally, we provide their explicit construction by attaching leaves to a core of internal vertices. Applying this framework, we obtain the complete characterization of extremal $Δ$-trees for the Degree-Ratio Sombor ($DRSO$), Symmetric Division Deg ($SDD$), and Hyperbolic Sombor ($HSO$) indices for all $Δ\ge 3$. Furthermore, the analytical conditions identify the exact degree thresholds for the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) and Diminished Sombor ($DSO$) indices, showing that the same extremal family maximizes $AG$ if and only if $3 \le Δ\le 8$, and $DSO$ if and only if $3 \le Δ\le 4$. Finally, since changing the edge count from $m = n - 1$ to $m = n - 1 + k$ affects only the constant term in the decomposition while leaving the penalty function $G(x,y)$ invariant, the method extends directly to connected $k$-cyclic graphs.

entry.title: On first-order limiting probabilities for small permutation classes
entry.summary: Given a small permutation class $\mathcal{P}$, we consider the set of possible limits of the probability $\mathbb{P}\big(\mathbfσ_n \models Ψ\big)$ that a uniformly chosen random permutation $\mathbfσ_n\in \mathcal{P}_n$ satisfies a fixed first-order sentence in Theory of Two Orders (TOTO). In the case of small permutation classes with polynomial growth, we show this limit set is finite, and characterize the set explicitly. In particular, we prove that many natural small permutation classes of polynomial growth arising from permutation matrices satisfy a $0$-$1$ convergence law, and have an infinite model. In the case of small permutation classes with exponential growth we show that the limit set is dense in $[0,1]$, thereby extending a result of Albert--Bouvel--Féray--Noy, using different methods, to this range.

entry.title: Optimal solution ranks in the Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation
entry.summary: For every $n$ and $r$ with $1\le r$ and $\binom{r+1}{2}\le n$, we construct a connected unweighted graph on $n$ vertices whose Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation has a unique optimal solution of rank $r$. The main examples are the Kneser graphs $K(m,2)$, whose unique optima have rank $m-1$. A six-vertex wheel supplies rank three, and attaching pendant vertices preserves both rank and uniqueness. For dense random graphs, we also prove a polynomial lower bound on the optimal rank.

entry.title: Sharp bounds for Duke--Erdős--Rödl problems on cycle-connected subgraphs
entry.summary: For $k\ge2$, a graph is $C_{2k}$-connected if every two distinct edges lie together on an even cycle of length at most $2k$ in that graph. Let $f_k(n,m)$ be the largest number of edges in a $C_{2k}$-connected subgraph that every $n$-vertex graph with $m$ edges must contain. In this paper, we study two cycle-connected problems raised by Duke, Erdős and Rödl. First, Duke, Erdős and Rödl showed that $f_3(n,\lfloor n^{2-β}\rfloor)=Θ(n^{2-3β})$ for every fixed $0< β<1/2$ and ask for the case of $β\ge 1/2$. We solve this problem in a stronger form by determining that the optimal range of $β$ is $(0,2/3]$. Second, we prove that $f_2(n,\binom n2-s)=(1/(2e)+o(1))n^3/s$ whenever $\frac{s}{n}\to\infty$ and $s=o(n^2)$, determining the leading constant in an estimate of Duke, Erdős, and Rödl. The first result uses a finite-field construction and a count of three-edge paths. The second uses the known structure of $C_4$-connected graphs and estimates for complete bipartite subgraphs in a random graph.

entry.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
entry.summary: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.

entry.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
entry.summary: We prove that for all $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the Lee ball $B_n(r)$ does not tile $\Z^n$ by translations, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets and completing the existence classification of perfect Lee codes in $\Z^n$. The proof combines translation-invariant averaging, boundary contact identities, and integer moment inequalities with coefficient comparisons in stable symmetric functions. Consequently, we obtain finite local obstructions, strict Banach density gaps for packings and coverings, and the nonexistence of exact measurable Lee-ball towers. In the lattice specialization, our result classifies the attainability of the Lee bound for even-degree abelian Cayley graphs, excludes normal topological coverings and Galois graph coverings for Lee-ball completions, and gives a strict node bound for lattice cubature as well as the nonexistence of subgroup-indexed orthogonal exponential bases on $B_n(r)$.

entry.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
Asymptotic Rank of Complete Graph Tensors
entry.summary: Graph tensors extend the matrix multiplication tensor by placing a two-party identity tensor on every edge of a graph and keeping one tensor leg at every vertex. We study the asymptotic rank of the tensor associated with the complete graph. For every integer $n\geq 2$, over the complex numbers, we prove \[ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor \leq \log_2\widetilde R\bigl(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)\bigr) \leq \frac{n^2}{4}. \] The upper bound matches the maximum-cut lower bound for every even $n$ and differs from it by only $1/4$ for every odd $n$. In particular, the exponent per edge is below $2/3$ for every $n\geq5$, answering a question of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. Our proof extends the polynomial multiplication approach underlying OpenAI's bound $ω\leq9/4$. The main step separates any fixed number of shared tensor legs simultaneously, using only linearly many direct-sum copies in the number of blocks. This yields an entropy inequality for higher-order tensors. We apply it to the tensor for multiplying $n-1$ polynomials, whose rank is linear in the input length. Discrete concavity and a shifted tripling inequality then force a lower bound on a symmetrized spectral profile. Comparing this growth with polynomial interpolation gives the stated upper bound while preserving all $n$ tensor legs. We also prove an operational barrier for these higher-order polynomial constructions. For $n\geq3$, the specified formal reduction rules cannot certify an exponent below $n^2/4$ for $\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)$, even after taking tensor powers and allowing subexponential overhead and common auxiliary factors. This extends the symmetric three-leg barrier of Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam and explains the remaining gap for odd complete graphs within this method.

entry.title: General-position sets and linear hypergraphs
entry.summary: We prove that every linear hypergraph on $N$ vertices with edge sizes $O(\sqrt N)$ and $O(N^2\log N)$ triples contained in its edges has a subset of size $Ω(\sqrt N)$ meeting each edge in at most two vertices. As an application, every set of $N$ planar points with at most $\sqrt N$ collinear points contains $Ω(\sqrt N)$ points in general position. This proves a conjecture of Payne and Wood and gives the optimal quadratic bound for a geometric Ramsey problem posed by Gowers.

entry.title: The \(\mathcal A_α\)-Spectral Turán Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
entry.summary: For fixed $r\geq3$ and $0<α<1$, we study the maximum $α$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graphs. Here $\mathcal A_{α,s}(G)=α\mathcal D_s(G)+(1-α)\mathcal A_s(G)$, where $\mathcal A_s(G)$ and $\mathcal D_s(G)$ are the adjacency and degree tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of $G$. For $s=r$, put $c_r=((r-1)/r)^{r-1}$. We prove that, for all sufficiently large $n$, the unique extremal graph is the Turán graph $T_r(n)$ if $α\leq c_r$, and $K_1\vee T_{r-1}(n-1)$ if $α>c_r$. For general $3\leq s\leq r$ and $n\geq r$, every extremal graph is complete $r$-partite. The asymptotic maximum $α$-$r$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graphs is $\max\{r^{1-r},α(r-1)^{1-r}\}n^{r-1}+o(n^{r-1})$. In every asymptotically extremal sequence of complete $r$-partite graphs, all parts have size $n/r+o(n)$ when $α<c_r$; when $α>c_r$, one part has size $o(n)$ and the remaining parts have size $n/(r-1)+o(n)$. At $α=c_r$, both part-size patterns are asymptotically extremal.

entry.title: Jónsson cardinals, Magidor cardinals, and the number of omitted colors
entry.summary: Let $λ$ be a Magidor cardinal and let $α\in[α_M,λ)$. We show that $λ\rightarrow[λ]^{\aleph_0-bd}_{α,<α}$. We prove the consistency of a similar statement for Jónsson cardinals.

entry.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
entry.summary: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

entry.title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
entry.summary: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps. We introduce generalized cubic partitions and discover the minimal excludant, as well as several additional results.

entry.title: A planar signed graph with circular chromatic number five
entry.summary: A circular $r$-coloring of a signed graph maps its vertices to a circle of circumference $r\ge2$, with the endpoints of negative edges at circular distance at least $1$ and those of positive edges at most $r/2-1$; the circular chromatic number is the infimum of such $r$. We construct a simple planar signed triangulation on $85$ vertices with circular chromatic number exactly $5$. This improves the lower bound on the supremum of the circular chromatic numbers of simple planar signed graphs from $14/3$ to $5$, giving a partial answer to a question posed by Naserasr, Wang, and Zhu.

entry.title: Minimum Distance Spectral Radius of Tree with Given Maximum Degree
entry.summary: In this article, the unique graph with minimum distance spectral radius among trees with given order $n$ and maximum degree $\varDelta$ is determined, where $2\varDelta+1 \leq n \leq \varDelta^{2} +1$ for $\varDelta \geq 3$. This article is a part proof of the conjecture proposed in $\cite{ref1}$.

entry.title: Spectral Turán problems for complete bipartite expansions in linear hypergraphs
entry.summary: An $r$-uniform hypergraph is linear if any two edges share at most one vertex. For a family $\mathcal F$ of $r$-graphs, let $\text{ex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ denote, respectively, the maximum number of edges and the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $\mathcal F$-free linear $r$-graph. In this paper, we show that for $t\ge s\ge3$, $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})\le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r-1}n^{1-1/s}+o(n^{1-1/s})$, where $K_{s,t}^{+}$ is the $r$-graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{s,t}$ by enlarging each edge with $r-2$ new vertices. This answers a problem of She, Fan and Kang in a stronger form. Moreover, our result implies that $\text{ex}^\text{lin}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+}) \le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r(r-1)}n^{2-1/s}+o(n^{2-1/s})$, which improves the leading coefficient in the corresponding bound of Gao and Chang. We also give a construction which implies that $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})=Θ(n^{1-1/s})$ and $\text{ex}^\text{lin}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})=Θ(n^{2-1/s})$ for $s\ge 4r-6$ and $t>(s-1)!$.

entry.title: Extremal 3-uniform hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles
entry.summary: Let $f_r(n)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph in which all disjoint pairs of edges have distinct unions. In 1977, Erdős posed the problem of determining $f_r(n)$ and, in particular, asked whether $f_3(n)=O(n^2)$. Füredi later proved that $\binom{n-1}{r-1}+\left\lfloor (n-1)/r\right\rfloor \le f_r(n)<\frac72\binom{n}{r-1}$ for $r\ge3$ and $n\ge2r$. Motivated by his constructions, he further conjectured that $f_3(n)\le\binom{n}{2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and that, for each fixed $r\ge4$, the lower bound is exact for all sufficiently large $n$. This is known as the Erdős--Füredi conjecture. In a recent breakthrough, Huang, Ma and Yang proved the conjecture for every fixed $r\ge4$ and characterized all extremal hypergraphs. In this paper, we settle the remaining $3$-uniform case for every $n$. The bound is sharp whenever $n\ge5$ and $n\equiv1,5\pmod{20}$. Our proof uses a local weight inequality and a transfer argument.

entry.title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
entry.summary: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $Γ$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $Γ$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $Γ$.

entry.title: Explicit weighing matrices $W(n,k)$ for all $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ with $4 \le n \le 108$, and all $1 \le k \le n$
entry.summary: We present an explicit weighing matrix $W(n,k)$ for every order $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ with $4\le n\le 108$ and every weight $1\le k\le n$: 1512 matrices in total, each checked in exact integer arithmetic. Of these, 961 come from classical constructions (identity, direct sums, Kronecker products, Paley matrices and skew-Hadamard doubling) and 551 are Goethals-Seidel matrices, found by exhaustive search (24 matrices, $n\le 24$) or by simulated annealing on the periodic autocorrelation cost (527 matrices, $n\ge 28$). The note is self-contained as far as the methods are concerned: it presents all the construction methods used and the algorithm that selects among them, explains the algorithm step by step, proves every identity on which the constructions rely, and illustrates each method with a matrix taken from the catalogue. It does not reproduce the 1512 matrices, which are available in the repository. It also gives a short parity obstruction to Goethals-Seidel matrices $W(4m,4m-1)$ with $m$ even, and lists the generating sequences of thirteen matrices whose parameters appear as unresolved in historical tables consulted by the author; their status in the current literature is still being checked, and no claim of priority is made.
entry.arxiv:comment: 32 pages. Code and data: https://github.com/adrianmaciasquintero/weighing-matrices (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23484194)

entry.title: Nilpotent Lie algebras of nilpotence class at most three via graphs
entry.summary: In this work, we associate with each finite simple graph $G$ a nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}_G$ of class at most three, whose underlying vector space has a basis indexed by the vertices, edges, and paths of length two of $G$. Its nilpotency class is exactly three if and only if $G$ contains a path of length two. We compute the dimensions of its lower central series and describe its center. Over fields of characteristic different from two, we prove that two such Lie algebras are isomorphic if and only if their underlying graphs are isomorphic. We also give an algebraic description using quotients involving exterior and symmetric squares. Finally, we study balanced blow-ups and prove that $\mathfrak{n}_G$ is a retract of $\mathfrak{n}_{G^{(m)}}$.

entry.title: Improved Bounds on Proportional Choice Numbers
entry.summary: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. We consider two previously posed questions regarding proportional choice numbers: (1) Is there a constant $C$ such that $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq C$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$? and (2) Is it the case that for any graph $G$, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G)+1$ where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$? In this paper we answer both questions: the first in the affirmative and the second in the negative. Specifically, we prove that $χ_{pc}(G) \leq 2^{χ'(G)}$ for every graph $G$ where $χ'(G)$ is the chromatic index of $G$. Consequently, $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq 4$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. We also prove that when $G$ is the disjoint union of $(a+b-1)$ copies of $K_{a,b}$, $χ_{pc}(G)=a+b$. In particular, for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a graph $G$ with $Δ(G)=m$ and $χ_{pc}(G)=2Δ(G)$.

entry.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
entry.summary: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.

entry.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
entry.summary: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2πi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
entry.arxiv:comment: 47 pages, 37 figures. This paper is the second one in a series of two. The first paper is available at arXiv:2610.28986

entry.title: On Lewis's homotopy in distance-regular graphs
entry.summary: In 2000, Lewis introduced a nested sequence of normal subgroups of the fundamental group of a distance-regular graph $Γ$. While the full homotopy group itself is simply a free group, it is interesting to determine the smallest integer $k$ such that every closed walk in $Γ$ can be built, up to homotopy, from closed walks of "essential length" $k$ or less. Lewis proved that $k\le 6$ for any $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $Γ$ that is not a pseudoquotient. In this paper, we prove that $k=3$ for Johnson graphs and that $k=4$ in the case of Hamming graphs. We also compute the homotopy groups of natural cell complexes associated to the folded Johnson graphs and folded cubes. The paper finishes with some open questions and suggestions for further lines of investigation.

entry.title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
entry.summary: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.

entry.title: The $\rm{v}$-number of $t$-closed neighborhood ideals
entry.summary: We give a combinatorial characterization of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal associated to a graph $G$, and investigate its relation with other invariants such as the $t$-domination number and the smallest size of a ball of radius $t$ in the graph $G$. We present several new cases where it is satisfied that the $\rm{v}$-number is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity. We analyze the behavior of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal with respect to the parameter $t$. Lastly, we compute explicit formulas for the $\rm{v}$-number in the case of paths, cycles, and caterpillars, and analyze the case of Hamming graphs.

entry.title: Between the Semi-Random Process and G(n,p)
entry.summary: We study a random graph process that connects the Erdős--Rényi random graph with the semi-random process. In each round, a uniformly random vertex is revealed together with a uniformly random candidate set of $s$ possible partners, and Builder chooses one of them. We study how this limited adaptivity $s$ changes the hitting times of monotone graph properties and how the familiar logarithmic ``coupon--collector'' delays in random graphs are reflected in this setting.

entry.title: Solving Large SDPs from Flag Algebra Problems
entry.summary: The flag algebra method is a general tool in extremal combinatorics, which has been useful in tackling open problems concerning graphs, hypergraphs, permutations, point sets, and other structures. The method establishes combinatorial inequalities via sums of squares, which are usually obtained by a semidefinite relaxation of the original combinatorial problem. A typical application of the method in graph theory starts with fixing a parameter $n$ followed by constructing a semidefinite program based on the (subgraph) structure of all $n$-vertex graphs. In the standard formulation before symmetry reductions, there is a coefficient constraint for every admissible $n$-vertex graph up to isomorphism. For 3-uniform hypergraphs, there are 2,136 of them on 6 vertices and 7,013,320 on 7 vertices. While solving the resulting program for $n=6$ is an easy task on any modern computer, the programs for $n = 7$ seems out of reach, mainly because the SDP solvers need too much RAM. Yet solving such programs for as large $n$ as possible is desirable because they typically yield better bounds for the original combinatorial problems. We bypass the aforementioned memory requirements by linear programming with cutting planes. Although we do not guarantee that this cutting-plane procedure reaches an optimum in finitely many iterations, in many flag algebra instances it uses much less memory and yields improved bounds for well-known hypergraph Turán problems. We use this method to obtain numerical bounds for Turán densities and codegree squared densities of several 3-uniform hypergraphs including the tetrahedron, where we obtained the upper bound 0.55753 and tetrahedron without one edge with a new upper bound 0.2865. It also allows to tackle bounds on Turán densities of 7-vertex 3-graphs using flag algebras, which was not possible before.

entry.title: Packing colourings of claw-free subcubic graphs
entry.summary: We prove that every claw-free subcubic graph admits a \packA-packing colouring, confirming a conjecture of Mortada, El Zein and Al Hajjar. The proof combines a reduction to line graphs of subdivided loopless cubic multigraphs with local colouring extensions. We also give a negative answer to their question on \packB-packing colourings by constructing an infinite family of connected bridgeless claw-free cubic counterexamples. The smallest graph in this family has 36 vertices. More generally, we characterise the simple cubic graphs whose triangle expansions admit a \packB-packing colouring in terms of gated independent odd-cycle transversals. This characterisation gives a classification for connected bridgeless claw-free cubic bases and shows that the double triangle expansion of a loopless cubic multigraph admits such a colouring if and only if the multigraph has a perfect matching.

entry.title: Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
entry.summary: Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$. Andrews proved that $A_r(n)=B_r(n)$ for all positive integers $r$ and nonnegative integers $n$, thereby recovering MacMahon's identity as the special case $r=1$. We derive generating functions and asymptotic formulas for the total numbers of hooks of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$ in both partition classes, employing Wright's circle method. These asymptotic formulas yield several hook length bias results. In particular, for sufficiently large $n$, the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $1$-hooks than the $A_r$-type partitions, whereas for hook lengths $2$ and $3$, the bias is reversed when $r=1$ and favors the $B_r$-type partitions when $r\geq 2$. We also establish asymptotic inequalities among hook numbers of different lengths within each partition class. Finally, for fixed hook lengths $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$, we prove that the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $\ell$-hooks than the $B_{r+1}$-type partitions for sufficiently large $n$. These results reveal systematic asymptotic patterns in the distribution of small hook lengths across the two partition families.

entry.title: Combinatorial models for Quasicrystals and Schur-Weyl Duality
entry.summary: Quasicrystals were defined by Cain and Malheiro and Maas-Gariépy to model the decomposition of Schur polynomials into fundamental quasisymmetric functions. We define a new combinatorial model for crystal graphs of type $A_{n-1}$, called parsed content words, for which the decomposition into quasicrystals is particularly evident. We use the model to describe a combinatorial interpretation of Schur-Weyl duality and recover the classical combinatorial proof of the well-known expansion of homogeneous symmetric functions into Schur functions within our framework.
